reason: The cited evidence (E1) discusses the general effect of titanium on microstructure and solid solution strengthening in AlCoCrFeNi-based HEAs, but provides no specific data on TiNi precipitate formation, aging response, or mechanical properties at 800 °C in a Ti-Ni-primary system. The key premises regarding precipitate type, size, distribution, and the resulting property improvements are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: TiNi (B2) intermetallic precipitates can form in a Ti-Ni-Co-Cr-Fe HEA matrix upon aging at 900 °C.
These precipitates will be nanoscale (10–50 nm) and uniformly dispersed.
The precipitates will increase elevated-temperature yield strength by 20–30% and improve creep resistance at ~800 °C via precipitation strengthening.
The baseline alloy (Ti35Ni35Co10Cr10Fe10) produced by spark plasma sintering is a single-phase or predominantly disordered matrix amenable to such precipitation.
